title: Sonny Stitt pressures Dizzy and Dizzy bows to him
summary: Stitt's long solo draws huge applause, so Dizzy answers with a long solo and takes his bow to Stitt.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: You know, cause there ain't nobody at that place, you know, they stand right there listening and listening at us play man, and uh, I remember one night uh, Sonny Stitt, you know how flamboyant he can get sometime.
Uhm, you know, he played both alto and uh, tenor so our repertory was the repertory Dizzy and Bird played.

So, Sonny Stitt, he was just going crazy one night man, he played a long time with the alto and he put the alto down and picked up the tenor you know, and he was playing and boy, and me and the rhythm section was like, boy, we was playing and playing so we was, when he had a thing he strolled a lot, when he get tired, he strolled so there wasn't nothing going but me and Jimmy Cobb, so he played and played and when the people applauded and applauded, see Dizzy still down, you know, just listening and looking at him, you know, just as calm, but Dizzy don't like nobody for to, to uh, put pressure on him...

You know, for, he don't like for people to put pressure on him uhm, so he figured that's what Son Stitt was doing to him you know, because all the people was applaud man, they went crazy, you know, so Dizzy brought the rhythm section down, volume-wise, and he start fiddling man, he got, he fiddled all through the horn and all the changes, I say oh, for I say about a good seven-eight choruses.
And there's a little step that he makes when he go up to that high C and he start walking that thing down from there boy.
And when he got through playing a solo man, they're a still applauding in Pittsburgh.

That's right, and uhm, he had a nickname they start calling him King of uh, cause that's all Sonny Stitt was saying while Dizzy was playing, 'Don't be so mean, King, don't---please don't be so mean, King'.

You know, and when Dizzy finished playing he didn't bow to no audience, he bowed to Sonny Stitt he took his bow to Sonny Stitt and so that stopped all that stuff, him putting that show on up on the stage.
You see, because you can get your feelings hurt up there, being around Dizzy.
